1.explanation:
• packages/components/src/components/code-snippet/code-snippet.js – This is the core web-component implementation of CodeSnippet; it needs to accept a disabled attribute, apply the correct CSS class for styling, and skip binding of focus/click handlers when disabled.  
• packages/react/src/components/CodeSnippet/CodeSnippet.js – The React wrapper currently ignores or does not fully implement the disabled prop. It must accept disabled, pass it through to the underlying web component (or rendered elements), and conditionally disable event handlers and focusability.  
• packages/react/src/components/CopyButton/CopyButton.js – The copy button inside CodeSnippet must also accept and honor a disabled prop (rendering a disabled <button> and blocking click/focus). CodeSnippet must forward its disabled state into this component.  
• packages/react/src/components/CodeSnippet/CodeSnippet-story.js – The Storybook story for CodeSnippet should be updated to include a disabled knob and showcase the new disabled style and behavior.  
• packages/react/src/components/CodeSnippet/CodeSnippet-test.js & CopyButton-test.js – Unit tests need to be extended to cover the new disabled prop: verifying that the snippet and copy button render with the disabled attribute/class, do not respond to clicks or keyboard events, and are not focusable when disabled=true.  
• packages/react/src/components/CodeSnippet/CodeSnippet.mdx – The documentation must be updated to document the new disabled prop in the API table and show examples of the disabled state.
1.bug_scenario: The ask is to add a true "disabled" state to the CodeSnippet component so that it can render as a non-interactive placeholder (greyed out, not focusable, with its copy button disabled) when its content isn’t yet available. In the screenshots, we can see that although the developer passed the prop disabled={true}, the CodeSnippet still looks and behaves as if it were enabled: it remains keyboard-focusable, the copy icon still responds to clicks, and the styling isn’t updated to convey a disabled state. The desired behavior is that when disabled is true, the snippet container and its internal copy button should be rendered in a disabled style and should not respond to any user interactions or focus.

2.explanation:
1. packages/components/src/code-snippet/code-snippet.config.js
   • Defines the JSON‐schema of the web component’s API. You’ll need to add a `disabled` attribute here so downstream frameworks (React, Angular, Vue) know that `disabled` is a valid prop/attribute on the core CodeSnippet element.
2. packages/components/src/code-snippet/code-snippet.js
   • The implementation of the vanilla/web‐component snippet. This is where you would observe the `disabled` attribute and toggle visual styles (e.g. add a `disabled` CSS class), remove tabindex, and prevent copy‐clicks when disabled.
3. packages/react/src/components/CodeSnippet/CodeSnippet.js
   • The React wrapper for the core snippet. You need to accept a `disabled` prop, pass it through to the underlying web component (or apply the flag in React), conditionally render `aria-disabled`, strip out `tabIndex`, and disable the embedded CopyButton.
4. packages/react/src/components/CodeSnippet/CodeSnippet.mdx
   • The documentation for the CodeSnippet component. Update the prop table and usage guidelines to include the new `disabled` boolean, describing its behavior and styling.
5. packages/react/src/components/CodeSnippet/CodeSnippet-story.js
   • The Storybook stories for CodeSnippet. Add a knob/select for `disabled` to demonstrate the disabled appearance and behavior.
6. packages/react/src/components/CodeSnippet/__tests__/CodeSnippet-test.js
   • The unit tests. Add tests asserting that when `disabled` is true, the snippet has no `tabindex`, the copy button is disabled, and clicking/copy events are no‐ops. This ensures the behavior is locked in moving forward.
2.bug_scenario: The screenshots show a <CodeSnippet> that the consumer has wired up with a `disabled` prop, but nothing in the component actually responds to it. When disabled is true, the snippet is still styled as active, still accepts keyboard focus, and the copy‐to‐clipboard button still works. The ask is to introduce a true “disabled” state on CodeSnippet so that: (1) the snippet is styled in a disabled/greyed out way, (2) it is not keyboard focusable, (3) its internal copy button is also disabled (no click or keyboard events).
